context.en: I'm going to travel to Beijing.

why: 要 + verb says what you plan to do: 我要去 means I am going to go.

not.最: 最 means 'most'; it needs an adjective or a liking verb.
not.也: 我也去 is grammatical, but means 'I also go', not 'going to'.
not.的: 的 cannot come before a verb here.

flag: 也 is grammatical here too (I also go to Beijing), though the English says 'going to'.

q: 我们___不要买几个新的椅子？

context.en: Should we buy some new chairs?

why: 要不要 is the yes/no form of 要. The blank plus 不要 must make 要不要.

not.想: 想不要 is not a pattern; it would be 想不想.
not.会: 会不要 is not a pattern; it would be 会不会.
not.能: 能不要 is not a pattern; it would be 能不能.

context.en: I like football most.

why: 最 + verb/adjective means 'the most': 最喜欢 is 'like best'.

not.要: 要 would mean 'want to', and 要喜欢 is odd.
not.太: 太喜欢 needs 了 at the end (太喜欢……了).
not.多: 多 asks 'how' before an adjective, not before 喜欢.

context.en: September is the best time to visit Beijing.

why: 最好 means 'the best'. 最 goes before the adjective 好 to say September is the best time.

not.太: 太好 needs 了 at the end.
not.要: 要好 does not give this meaning.
not.都: 都好 means 'all are good', not 'best'.

context.rule: 几 = a few; number + measure + 多 = more than
context.en: It's over six months old.

why: Number + measure word + 多 means 'more than': 六个多月 is 'over six months'.

not.几: 几 cannot follow 六个 as a number.
not.最: 最 cannot sit between 个 and 月.
not.少: 六个少月 is not Chinese; 少 cannot follow 个 like this.

context.rule: 几 = a few; number + measure + 多 = more than
context.en: I want to buy a few books.

why: 几 asks or says a small number: 几本书 is 'a few books'.

not.多: 多本书 is not used for 'a few'.
not.最: 最本书 is not a phrase; 最 needs an adjective or verb.
not.每: 每本书 means 'every book', not 'a few'.

context.rule: 是不是: “isn't it?” — checking a guess
context.en: You rarely get sick — do you like sport?

why: 是不是 checks a guess: the speaker thinks you like sport because you rarely get sick.

not.为什么: 为什么 asks the reason, which does not fit.
not.怎么样: 怎么样 asks 'how is it', not a yes/no check.
not.多少: 多少 asks for an amount.

context.rule: 每 + measure word … 都: every
context.en: I get up at six every day.

why: 每 + 天 means 'every day'. 每天六点 says every day at six.

not.都: 都天 is not a word; 都 means 'all'.
not.多: 多天 is not used for 'every day'.

context.rule: 每 + measure word … 都: every
context.en: He goes running every morning.

why: 每天早上 already means 'every morning'; 都 adds 'always' before the verb 去.

not.每: 每 is already used in 每天; 每去 is wrong.
not.也: 也去 is grammatical, but means 'also goes'; 每 pairs with 都.
not.最: 最 means 'most' and does not fit here.

flag: 也 is grammatical too (he also goes running every morning); the English and the 每……都 pattern point to 都.

context.rule: 多大 / 多高: how old / how tall
context.en: How tall is your brother?

why: 多 + adjective asks degree: 多高 means 'how tall'.

not.几: 几 asks small counts, not height.
not.最: 最高 would be a statement, not a question.

context.rule: 多大 / 多高: how old / how tall
context.en: How old are you this year?

why: 多大 asks age: 'how old'. 多 goes before the adjective 大.

not.几: 几大 is wrong; 几岁 asks a small child's age.
not.太: 太大 means 'too big', not a question.
not.很: 很大 means 'very big', not a question.

context.rule: 我的 / 昨天的 / 红色的: “the … one”
context.en: Is this watch yours?

why: Noun + 的 can stand for the thing: 你的 means 'yours', so 是你的吗 asks if it is yours.

not.了: 了 shows a change or finished action, not ownership.
not.呢: 呢 does not come before 吗.
not.吧: 吧 makes a guess and cannot sit before 吗.

context.rule: 我的 / 昨天的 / 红色的: “the … one”
context.en: The red one on the left is mine.

why: Adjective + 的 makes a phrase for the thing: 红色的 means 'the red one'.

not.了: 了 cannot turn 红色 into a noun.
not.吗: 吗 ends a question; it cannot sit in the middle.
not.着: 着 goes after verbs; 红色 is not a verb.

context.en: Let me have a look.

why: Verb + 一下 makes the action short and light: 看一下 is 'take a quick look'.

not.一点儿: 一点儿 means 'a little' of something, not a short action.
not.一次: 一次 counts times, not a quick try.

context.en: Your daughter's room is so pretty!

why: 真 + adjective shows feeling: 真漂亮 is 'so pretty!'.

not.最: 最漂亮 is grammatical, but means 'the prettiest'.
not.多: 多漂亮 can say 'how pretty!', but usually with 啊; 真 is the pattern.

flag: 最 and 多 can also fit grammatically (the prettiest / how pretty!); 真 is the best match.

context.rule: 是 + who + verb + 的: stresses who did it
context.en: This book was written by me.

why: 是……的 stresses who did it: 是我写的 means 'it was me who wrote it'.

not.在: 在 shows location, not who did it.

context.rule: 是 + who + verb + 的: stresses who did it
context.en: Who made the call?

why: 是谁打的 uses 是……的 to ask who made the call; 是 can be dropped in speech but 的 stays.

not.了: 了 cannot end a 是……的 sentence.
not.吗: 吗 does not follow 谁.
not.呢: 呢 does not complete this pattern.

q: 我十一岁___时候开始踢足球。

context.en: I started football when I was eleven.

why: …的时候 means 'when …'. 的 links the clause 我十一岁 to 时候.

not.了: 了 cannot link a clause to 时候.
not.得: 得 follows verbs, not a clause.

context.en: I've already studied Chinese for two years.

why: 已经 + 了 means 'already': 已经学了两年了 is 'already studied for two years'.

not.正在: 正在 means 'in the middle of', not a past amount.
not.还: 还 means 'still' and does not fit 学了两年.
not.就: 就 does not mean 'already' with a time length here.

context.en: He has already gone home.

why: 已经……了: 了 at the end shows the action has happened, so 已经回家了 is 'has gone home'.

not.的: 的 does not show a completed action here.

context.en: This one's good, so take this one.

why: 就 + verb shows a quick decision: since this one is good, 就买这件 means 'then take this one'.

not.再: 再 means 'again/later', not a decision now.
not.才: 才 means 'only then', which sounds late.

q: 颜色___可以，就是有点儿大。

context.rule: 还可以 / 还好: OK, passable
context.en: The colour's OK, but it's a bit big.

why: 还可以 is a set phrase meaning 'OK, passable'.

not.就: 就可以 means 'then it is fine', not 'passable'.
not.再: 再可以 is not a phrase.
not.最: 最可以 is not a phrase.

context.en: This garment is a bit big.

why: 有点儿 + adjective means 'a bit', often unwanted: 有点儿大 is 'a bit too big'.

not.一点儿: 一点儿 comes after an adjective (大一点儿).

context.en: I've been a bit tired lately.

why: 有点儿累 means 'a bit tired', a small complaint about how you feel.

not.一点儿: 累一点儿 puts 一点儿 after the adjective.
not.很多: 很多 cannot go before 累.

context.en: Why did you stop eating?

why: 怎么 + verb asks 'why/how come'; 怎么不吃了 asks why you stopped eating.

not.什么: 什么 asks 'what', so 什么不吃 is odd.

context.rule: 天天 / 个个 / 件件 … 都: every
context.en: This week I eat lamb every day.

why: 天天 means 'every day', and 天天都 stresses it: 'every day this week I eat lamb'.

not.天: 天 alone is not 'every day' before 都.
not.每: 每 needs a measure word: 每天都.
not.都: 都都 would repeat 都, which is already after the blank.

q: 这儿的衣服件件___很漂亮。

context.rule: 天天 / 个个 / 件件 … 都: every
context.en: Every garment here is pretty.

why: Doubled measure word + 都 means 'every one': 件件都 is 'every garment'.

context.en: Because it rained yesterday, none of us went.

why: 因为 starts the reason, and 所以 starts the result. The first part gives the reason: it rained.

not.所以: 所以 starts the result, not the reason.

q: 因为他每天跑步，___身体很好。

context.en: He runs every day, so he's healthy.

why: 所以 starts the result of the reason 因为他每天跑步: his body is healthy.

not.因为: 因为 is already used for the reason.

q: 已经9点多了，他怎么___在学习？

context.rule: 还在 … / 还没: still / not yet
context.en: It's past nine; why is he still studying?

why: 怎么还在学习 means 'why is he still studying', since it is already past nine.

not.也: 怎么也在学习 means 'why is he also studying'; it ignores the late time.

context.rule: time + 就 + verb: as soon as that
context.en: I'll be there in twenty minutes.

why: Time + 就 + verb shows it will happen soon: 二十分钟就到 is 'there in only twenty minutes'.

not.才: 才到 is grammatical, but means 'not until then', so it sounds late.

flag: 才 is grammatical too (only after twenty minutes, so it seems long); the English says 'soon', so 就 fits.

context.rule: A 离 B 远 / 近: distance from
context.en: Is your home far from the company?

why: A 离 B 远 means 'A is far from B': 你家离公司远吗.

not.从: 从 marks a starting point of movement, not distance.

q: ___我的生日还有一个多星期呢！

context.rule: A 离 B 远 / 近: distance from
context.en: My birthday is still over a week away!

why: 离 can measure time too: 离我的生日还有一个多星期 means 'over a week until my birthday'.

not.从: 从 marks a start point, not time left.

q: 坐公共汽车要一个多小时___！

context.en: It takes over an hour by bus, you know!

why: 呢 at the end of a statement adds emphasis: 要一个多小时呢 is 'it takes over an hour, you know'.

not.吗: 吗 would turn it into a question.
not.吧: 吧 suggests a guess or suggestion.
not.的: 的 does not give emphasis here.

context.en: Shall we see a movie this afternoon?

why: 好吗？ after a suggestion asks 'is that OK?': 我们下午去看电影，好吗？

not.是吗: ……，是吗？ checks a fact ('right?'); it does not suggest a plan.

context.en: Let me think, then I'll tell you.

why: 再 + verb means 'then, later': first think, then tell you.

not.就: 就 means 'right away'; for 'first think, then tell', use 再.

q: 王老师___我给大卫打个电话。

context.point: 让 / 叫 / 请 + person + verb
context.en: Teacher Wang asked me to call David.

why: 让 + person + verb means 'ask/let someone do': 让我打电话.

context.point: 让 / 叫 / 请 + person + verb
context.en: I'll send someone to have a look.

why: 叫 + person + verb means 'send/ask someone to do': 叫人去看看.

not.给: 给人去 does not give this meaning.
not.对: 对人去 is wrong; 对 means 'towards'.

q: 外边天气很好，我们出去运动___吧！

context.rule: 看看 / 想想 / 运动运动: briefly, casually
context.en: Nice weather — let's get some exercise!

why: Repeating a verb softens it: 运动运动 means 'do some exercise'. The 吧 then suggests it.

not.一下: 运动一下吧 is also fine; here the doubled verb is the pattern.
not.一点儿: 一点儿 means 'a little' of something.
not.了: 了 does not suit a suggestion with 吧.

flag: 一下 also works (运动一下吧); the question tests the doubled verb.

context.rule: 看见 / 听懂 / 做完 / 找到
context.en: Too many questions; I didn't finish.

why: Verb + 完 means finished: 没做完 is 'did not finish doing'.

not.见: 没做见 is wrong; 见 goes with 看/听.
not.懂: 没做懂 is wrong; 懂 goes with 看/听.
not.到: 没做到 means 'did not manage to do', a different meaning.

context.rule: 看见 / 听懂 / 做完 / 找到
context.en: Did you understand everything?

why: 听懂 means 'hear and understand'. The question asks if you understood everything.

not.完: 听完 is grammatical, but means 'finished listening', not 'understood'.
not.到: 听到 is grammatical, but means 'heard', not 'understood'.
not.见: 听见 is grammatical, but means 'heard', not 'understood'.

flag: 听完, 听到 and 听见 all give grammatical questions (finished / heard everything); only the English 'understand' points to 懂.

context.rule: 看见 / 听懂 / 做完 / 找到
context.en: David found a job.

why: 找到 means 'look for and find'. The result complement 到 shows success.

not.懂: 找懂 is wrong; 懂 is for understanding.
not.错: 找错 means 'looked in the wrong place' or 'found the wrong one'.

context.en: Starting work from next Monday.

why: 从 marks the starting time: 从下个星期一开始 means 'starting from next Monday'.

not.离: 离 shows distance between two points.

context.en: This is his first job.

why: 第 + number makes an ordinal: 第一个 is 'the first one'.

context.en: Stop watching TV; there's class tomorrow.

why: 不要……了 means 'stop doing': 不要看电视了 is 'don't watch TV any more'.

not.不是: 不是 denies a fact, not an action.
not.没有: 没有 denies a past action.

context.en: Stop looking — the phone's on the table.

why: 别 + verb + 了 means 'stop doing it': 别找了 tells someone to stop looking.

not.不: 不找了 says 'I will not look', not a command.
not.再: 再找了 is wrong; it would be 别再找了.

flag: 不找了 is grammatical too (I'm not going to look any more); 别 fits the 'Stop' meaning.

context.rule: A 对 B 有帮助 / 很好: for, towards
context.en: Watching TV helps with learning Chinese.

why: A 对 B 有帮助 means 'A helps B': 对学汉语有帮助.

context.rule: 正在 + verb: in the middle of doing
context.en: Mom is making lunch right now!

why: 正在 + verb + 呢 shows an action happening now: 正在准备午饭呢.

not.就要: 就要 means 'about to' and needs 了 at the end, not 呢.

q: 昨天和你一起唱歌___人是谁？

context.en: Who sang with you yesterday?

why: Verb phrase + 的 + noun describes the noun: 和你一起唱歌的人 is 'the person who sang with you'.

not.地: 地 links a describing word to a verb, not to a noun like 人.
not.得: 得 comes after a verb to say how; it cannot link to 人.
not.了: 了 cannot join a phrase to a noun.

context.en: He's three years older than me.

why: A 比 B + adjective + amount compares two things: 他比我大三岁.

not.和: 和 means 'and'; it does not compare this way.

q: 今天的西瓜比昨天便宜___。

context.en: Today's watermelon is a bit cheaper than yesterday.

why: A 比 B + adjective + 一些 means 'a bit more': 便宜一些 is 'a bit cheaper'.

not.一下: 一下 follows verbs, not adjectives like 便宜.
not.有点儿: 有点儿 goes before an adjective, not after.
not.很: 很 cannot follow 比 + adjective.

context.en: Watermelon isn't as cheap as apples.

why: A 没有 B + adjective means 'A is not as … as B': 西瓜没有苹果便宜.

not.不: 不苹果便宜 is not Chinese.
not.没: 没苹果便宜 is missing 有.
not.不是: 不是苹果便宜 is not Chinese.

context.en: You probably don't know her.

why: 可能 means 'maybe/probably': 你可能不认识她.

not.能: 能不认识 does not mean 'probably'.
not.会: 会不认识 does not mean 'probably' here.
not.可以: 可以不认识 means 'may not know', about permission.

context.en: You're wearing too little.

why: Verb + 得 + adjective says how: 穿得太少了 means 'dressed too thin'.

not.的: 你穿的 would mean 'what you wear'; to say how you dress, use 得.
not.了: 了 cannot be followed by 太少 here.

context.en: He speaks Chinese very well.

why: 说得很好: after 得, 很 + adjective says how well. 'Speaks very well.'

not.太: 太好 needs 了 (太好了).
not.最: 说得最好 is grammatical, but means 'speaks the best'.
not.更: 说得更好 is grammatical, but means 'speaks even better'.

flag: 最 (speaks the best) and 更 (speaks even better) are also grammatical; only the English 'very well' points to 很.

q: 他也希望能住___近一点儿。

context.en: He also hopes to live a bit closer.

why: 住得近一点儿: 得 links the verb 住 to the adjective result 近.

not.的: 的 does not link a verb and its result.

context.rule: A 比 B + verb + 得 + adjective
context.en: My wife cooks better than me.

why: A 比 B + verb + 得 + adjective compares ways: 比我做得好 is 'cooks better than me'.

not.跟: 跟 needs 一样 to compare.
not.和: 和 needs 一样 to compare.

context.en: The door is open, come in.

why: 门开着 describes a door that is still open. 着 shows a continuing state.

not.了: 了 shows a change, not a state.
not.得: 得 links a verb to a result.

context.en: What about the one holding a pencil?

why: 拿着铅笔 means 'holding a pencil'. 着 shows the hand is still holding it.

not.了: 拿了 means 'took', a finished action, not 'holding'.

context.en: Doesn't she already have a boyfriend?

why: 不是……吗 is a reminder: she surely already has a boyfriend, right?

not.是不是: 是不是 cannot be followed by 吗.
not.没有: 没有有 is not Chinese; 没有 cannot go before 有.

context.en: Go straight ahead from here.

why: 往 + direction means 'towards': 往前走 is 'walk forward'.

context.en: Have you seen that movie?

why: Verb + 过 shows experience: 看过 means 'have seen before'. 没有 in the question asks yes/no.

not.了: 看了……没有 is grammatical, but asks 'did you watch', not experience.
not.完: 看完 is grammatical, but asks 'did you finish watching'.

flag: 看了 and 看完 also make natural questions (did you watch / finish watching it?); only the English 'Have you seen' points to 过.

context.en: I've never been to China.

why: 没 + verb + 过 means 'never': 没去过中国 is 'have never been to China'.

not.了: 了 does not go with 没 here.

context.en: Although it's sunny, it's cold.

why: 虽然 starts the first part, 'although it is sunny', and 但是 starts the contrast.

not.但是: 但是 starts the contrast, not the first part.

q: 虽然有点儿贵，___我很喜欢。

context.en: Although a bit pricey, I love it.

why: 虽然……，但是……: after 'although it is a bit pricey', 但是 introduces the contrast: I love it.

not.虽然: 虽然 is already used at the start.

q: 我在这个商店买过一___东西。

context.en: I've bought something in this shop once.

why: 买过一次东西 means 'bought things there once'. 次 counts how many times.

not.个: 一个东西 is also grammatical (one thing) but not 'once'.
not.下: 一下东西 is wrong; 下 follows verbs.
not.件: 一件东西 is also grammatical (one item) but not 'once'.

flag: 个 and 件 also give grammatical sentences (one thing/item); 次 matches 'once' in the English.

context.en: The New Year is almost here!

why: 快要……了 means 'about to'. 了 ends the sentence and shows the change is near.

not.的: 的 does not show a coming change.

context.en: We're going back home next month.

why: 就要……了 means 'about to': 下个月就要回国了. 就要 fits a time marker like next month.

not.快: With a time word like 下个月, use 就要; 快(要)……了 does not take one.

context.en: We've already waited half an hour for her!

why: 都……了 shows impatience about time: 都等了半个小时了 is 'already waited half an hour'.

not.就: 就 means 'then/only', which loses the impatience.

context.en: It's already 8:40!

why: 都 + time + 了 means 'it is already …': 了 closes the time statement.

not.的: 的 does not close a time statement.
not.呢: 都……了 needs 了; 呢 does not close this pattern.
